Update endpoints are critical attack vectors as they may lack signature verification, allowing malicious code injection through compromised update channels.
Plugin update mechanisms often have weaker security controls than initial installations and may be vulnerable to man-in-the-middle or supply chain attacks.
Tool schemas define the interface between extensions and the core system, potentially exposing privilege escalation paths or undocumented capabilities that bypass security controls.
MCP tool listings may reveal available extensions with elevated permissions or cross-platform capabilities that could be exploited for lateral movement or privilege escalation.
Direct secrets endpoints often contain API keys, tokens, or credentials used for extension authentication and cross-service communication.
